Section 181.001 defines covered entities more broadly than federal HIPAA, expressly encompassing specified handling of protected health information by entities that can include computer-management businesses and Internet-site operators. Section 181.004 separately addresses federal and state coverage. Whether the particular information and conduct meet the state requirements—and whether exemptions apply—still needs examination, but “not a federal HIPAA covered entity” does not answer the Texas question. citeturn403321view0

There are federal consumer-protection routes outside HIPAA as well. The FTC’s finalized BetterHelp order addressed allegations that sensitive health information was shared contrary to privacy promises. Separately, the FTC’s Health Breach Notification Rule can cover qualifying personal-health-record products and related entities, including unauthorized disclosures rather than only hacking. Neither authority automatically applies to every chatbot interaction; both belong in a properly scoped assessment of the actual product and data flows. citeturn810661search1turn651980search6

One distinction remains important: **reproducing your information to you is not the same event as exposing it to an unauthorized recipient.** Collection, inference, retention, internal use, and external disclosure also need to be examined separately. Applicable breach rules turn on such matters as impermissible use or disclosure, authorization, recipients, and the regulated relationship—not merely the presence of medical language. citeturn651980search2turn651980search6

That is how we determine *which problem occurred*. It is not a reason to downgrade the information’s significance.
